problem:
Suppose we wish to calculate the Laplace transform 

$$
L{{t}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡4t}.
$$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below. You may make use of the following result:

$$
L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡\omega t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}},\,s>\omega .
$$

Let $f(t)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡4t$ and $F(s)=L{f(t)}.$ By the smoothness property of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
L{{t}^{2}f(t)}={{field-1}}.
$$

The Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is

$$
F(s)=L{f(t)}={{field-2}},\,s>4.
$$

We have that

$$
{F}^{″}(s)={{field-3}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
L{{t}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡4t}={{field-4}},\,s>4.
$$
worked_solution:
If a function $f(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty )$ and has exponential order $a,$ then its Laplace transform

$$
F(s)=L{f(t)}
$$

exists for every real $s>a,$ and $F$ is infinitely differentiable in this region of convergence. Moreover, for each integer $n\ge 0$ and every such $s,$ we have

$$
L{{t}^{n}f(t)}=(-1)^{n}{F}^{(n)}(s).
$$

In particular, for $n=2,$ we have

$$
L{{t}^{2}f(t)}={F}^{″}(s).
$$

We have that $f(t)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡4t.$ Using the given result with $\omega =4,$ the Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is 

$$
F(s)=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-16},\,s>4.
$$

Differentiating with respect to $s,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-16}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(s({s}^{2}-16)^{-1}) \\  & =({s}^{2}-16)^{-1}+s(-({s}^{2}-16)^{-2}\cdot 2s) \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}-16}{({s}^{2}-16)^{2}}-\frac{2{s}^{2}}{({s}^{2}-16)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{{s}^{2}+16}{({s}^{2}-16)^{2}} \\ {F}^{″}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{{s}^{2}+16}{({s}^{2}-16)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{{s}^{2}+16}{({s}^{2}-16)^{2}}) \\  & =-(\frac{({s}^{2}+16)^{′}\cdot ({s}^{2}-16)^{2}-({s}^{2}+16)\cdot {(({s}^{2}-16)^{2})}^{′}}{({s}^{2}-16)^{4}}) \\  & =-(\frac{(2s)({s}^{2}-16)^{2}-({s}^{2}+16)\cdot 2({s}^{2}-16)\cdot 2s}{({s}^{2}-16)^{4}}) \\  & =-(\frac{2s({s}^{2}-16)^{2}-4s({s}^{2}+16)({s}^{2}-16)}{({s}^{2}-16)^{4}}) \\  & =-(\frac{2s({s}^{2}-16)-4s({s}^{2}+16)}{({s}^{2}-16)^{3}}) \\  & =-(\frac{2{s}^{3}-32s-4{s}^{3}-64s}{({s}^{2}-16)^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{2{s}^{3}+96s}{({s}^{2}-16)^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the quotient rule to find ${F}^{″}(s).$

Therefore, by the smoothness property,

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡4t}={F}^{″}(s)=\frac{2{s}^{3}+96s}{({s}^{2}-16)^{3}},\,s>4.\end{aligned}
$$
